excerpts.text: Amendment Twenty-seven to the Constitution was ratified on May 7, 1992.
Michigan became the thirty-eighth state to ratify the amendment on May 7, 1992, thereby making it the Twenty-seventh Amendment, two-hundred years after it was originally created.

assessment.rationale: The Wikipedia article states the Twenty-seventh Amendment (Congressional Pay Amendment) was effective May 5, 1992, and that it was ratified over 202 years after initial proposal. Span 86 identifies it as the Congressional Pay Amendment. Span 91 confirms effective May 5, 1992.
assessment.provenance_note: Wikipedia article identifies the amendment and its 1992 effective date.
limitations: Wikipedia secondary source, not a primary constitutional record

excerpts.text: The **Twenty-seventh Amendment** (**Amendment XXVII**, also known as the **Congressional Pay Amendment** or the **Congressional Compensation Act of 1789**)[[1]](#cite_note-1) to the [United States Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Constitution "United States Constitution") states that any law that increases or decreases the salary of members of [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") may take effect only after the next election of the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") has occurred.

He later launched a nationwide campaign to complete its ratification.[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-:3-3) The amendment eventually became part of the United States Constitution, effective May 5, 1992.[[4]](#cite_note-:1-4)

assessment.rationale: Spans 119 and 120 document the original 1789 proposal and early state ratifications (seven states by 1792, Ohio 1873, Wyoming 1978), showing the amendment lay dormant for decades before resurgence in 1982.
assessment.provenance_note: Historical ratification timeline from the article.
limitations: Only partial ratification history, not the 1992 effective date

excerpts.text: The article on Congressional compensation was initially ratified by seven states through 1792 (including Kentucky), but was not ratified by another state for eighty years. The [Ohio General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_General_Assembly "Ohio General Assembly") ratified it on May 6, 1873, in protest of an unpopular [Congressional pay raise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salary_Grab_Act "Salary Grab Act").[[14]](#cite_note-dean-14) A century later, on March 6, 1978, the [Wyoming Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming_Legislature "Wyoming Legislature") also ratified the article.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

assessment.rationale: Span 138 notes Maine and Colorado ratified in April 1984 as part of Watson's campaign, illustrating the modern ratification sequence leading to 1992 effective date.
assessment.provenance_note: First modern ratifications under Watson's campaign.
limitations: Only two states; does not itself establish the 1992 effective date

excerpts.text: In April 1983, Maine became the first state to ratify the amendment as a result of Watson's campaign, followed by Colorado in April 1984.

assessment.rationale: Spans 216 and 217 confirm the 102nd Congress validated the amendment on May 20, 1992, with unanimous Senate and overwhelming House vote, establishing formal federal recognition of the 1992 effective date.
limitations: Congressional resolution, not the constitutional effective date itself

excerpts.text: On May 20, 1992, under the authority recognized in *Coleman*, and in keeping with the precedent established by [the ratification of the Fourteenth Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution#Adoption "Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution"), each house of the 102nd Congress passed its own version of a [concurrent resolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrent_resolution "Concurrent resolution") agreeing that the amendment was validly ratified, despite the more than 202 years the task took. The Senate's approval of the resolution was unanimous (99 to 0) and the House vote was 414 to 3.[[14]](#cite_note-dean-14)

assessment.rationale: Span 90 states the amendment was proposed in 1789, forgotten until 1982 when student Gregory Watson claimed it could still be ratified, launching a nationwide campaign.
limitations: Student claim, not independent verification of the 1992 effective date

excerpts.text: The proposed congressional pay amendment was largely forgotten until 1982, when Gregory Watson, a 19-year-old student at the [University of Texas at Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_at_Austin "University of Texas at Austin"), wrote a paper for a government class in which he claimed that the amendment could still be ratified.
